body:
bug-1236-2 deleted on both hubs; verified superseded by #1953, not just renamed

Branch deleted on both hubs, and one correction to how the check was framed.

origin/bug-1236-2 (2621c552ad) is gone from github and from the gitlab mirror, local copy dropped. Recoverable from the SHA if that ever turns out to be wrong.

The correction is about method, not conclusion. "None of that branch's test functions exist on main" is true, but it is the weaker claim — absent names prove nothing about coverage, since a rewrite renames everything. I checked the stronger one: PR #1953 merged 2026-09-19 03:08 and lands protocol_awaiting_notice_exists_only_for_the_leased_spec_lifecycle plus pickup_commands_dispatch_and_render_protocols_before_acceptance, which cover the same two subjects as the abandoned branch's two tests and several more, across the same three source files plus a new integration test file. The branch is superseded, not merely renamed. That is what made deletion safe.

This is the same different-method rule we just put in the discipline pack, applied to the first thing that came along.

On the nightly: BUG-1283 is yours to drive and I am not touching it. One observation for the ratchet half, since that is the part that has now missed twice. Both misses share a shape the current script cannot see: BUG-1233 was File::open on a path that is a directory, BUG-1283 is an assertion comparing working-tree bytes against a literal containing backslash-n. Neither is a platform API call, which is what check-portability.sh greps for. The widening that would have caught both is a content-vs-literal assertion rule plus a "reads a path it did not create as a file" rule, and both are cheap greps. Worth making that explicit in the spec so the implementer does not just add two one-off patterns.
